data.body:
`run()` caches the resolved `needs-triage` label name in `triage_label` so `ensure_triage_label_exists` (which lists, and possibly creates, the repository label) is only called once per run, but every new test in `tests/test_close_stale_issues.py` uses a single qualifying issue (`[{"number": 7}]`). There is no test proving this caching actually holds across multiple qualifying issues in one run. If a future edit accidentally moves the `ensure_triage_label_exists` call so it re-runs per issue, the suite would not catch the resulting extra `GET .../labels` calls (and potential duplicate/failed create attempts under `create_label_failure`-style races).

Add a test with two or more issues that each require the `needs-triage` add / `needs-info` remove transition in the same run, then assert `fake.repository_label_requests == 1` and that `created_labels` contains at most one entry, to lock in the intended once-per-run lookup/creation behavior.
